case_title: Sanjai Tiwari v. The State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.420, s.467, s.468, s.471, s.477A and s.120B; Prevention of Corruption Act s.13(1) r/w. s.13(2)
high_court_outcome: Directed trial court to expedite the criminal trial
neutral_facts: The accused was involved in a criminal case under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 477A, and 120B of the IPC, as well as Sections 13(1) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The Vigilance Department initiated an inquiry against the accused after a complaint was filed. The case was delayed due to a writ petition filed by the accused challenging the inquiry. The High Court directed the trial court to expedite the proceedings. However, an application was filed by a third party, who claimed to be a social activist, seeking to expedite the trial. The High Court dismissed the application, finding that the applicant had no locus standi to file such a petition. The trial court had not yet framed charges as of the date of the judgment.
